name: Speed
description: Speed is a frantic two-player shedding card game where players race to get rid of all their cards onto two central piles. Play is simultaneous and real-time. Cards can be played if they are one rank higher or lower (e.g., 6 on 5, or 6 on 7) than the card on the pile. There are no turns. The first player to exhaust their hand and draw pile shouts 'Speed!' to win.

content.text: Speed is a frantic two-player shedding card game where players race to get rid of all their cards onto two central piles. Play is simultaneous and real-time. Cards can be played if they are one rank higher or lower (e.g., 6 on 5, or 6 on 7) than the card on the pile. There are no turns. The first player to exhaust their hand and draw pile shouts 'Speed!' to win.

Speed is an American shedding game of the competitive patience family, related to Spit. It developed in the 20th century as a quicker, simpler variant and is widely played in schools and homes in the United States; it has regional names such as Super-spit, Spit 2, and Rush.
Standard 52-card Anglo-American deck; the full pack is used and dealt between the two players (five to hand, 15 to stock each, and two center piles of six).

Each player is dealt five cards to form a hand and 15 cards face down to the side as a draw pile. Two six-card piles are then dealt in the center, face down.

items.text: Jokers as wild: Jokers may be played as any rank; when played they act as the rank played on. A joker cannot be the last card played.
Three- or four-hand Speed: With three players, each gets five side-pile cards and three face-down center cards; remainder dealt as draw piles. With four players often two decks are used.
